'''Andor Kertész''' ({{IPA|hu|ˈɒndor ˈkɛrteːs|lang}}; 19 February 1929 – 3 April 1974) was a [[Hungarians|Hungarian]] [[mathematician]] and professor of mathematics at the [[University of Debrecen|Lajos Kossuth University]] (KLTE), [[Debrecen]]. He is the father of [[Linguistics|linguist]] [[András Kertész]].

==Biography and career==
Kertész was born on 19 February 1929 in [[Gyula (town)|Gyula]], [[Békés County]], Hungary.

He graduated from the Roman Catholic Secondary Grammar School at Gyula in 1947.

He earned [[Master of Science|M.Sc.]] degrees at [[University of Debrecen|Lajos Kossuth University]] (KLTE), [[Debrecen]] in [[Mathematics]], [[Physics]], and [[Descriptive geometry]] in 1952.

During his academic years he also worked as a demonstrator and then as an [[Internship|intern]] at the Institute of Mathematics of the KLTE and he became an [[aspirant]] of [[professor]]s [[Tibor Szele]] and [[László Rédei]] in [[Abstract algebra|Modern algebra]] in 1951 and since his graduation.

In 1954 he was appointed to an [[assistant professor]] at the Institute of Mathematics, KLTE.

He took the [[Candidate of Sciences|candidate]] (C.Sc.) of Mathematics degree in 1954 and was awarded [[Doctor of Science]] (D.Sc.) degree in mathematics in 1957.<ref>See Huynh (2010).</ref>

From 1960 until 1968 he acted as head of the Department of Algebra and Number Theory, Institute of Mathematics but as an [[associate professor]] ([[docent]], [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]]) just until 1963.

From 1961 until 1963, and from 1968 to 1971, he was a visiting professor at the [[Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg]], [[East Germany]].

In 1962, he lectured in the [[United Kingdom]] and [[West Germany]].

In 1963 he received the title of  [[professor|university (full) professor]] at the KLTE.

He was elected to full membership of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] in 1968.

In his memory and honour they established the Andor Kertész County Memorial Competition in Mathematics in 1988.

His papers were issued in both national and international prestigious professional research scientific journals, and numerous scientific articles and books were published.

He presented his talks at several conferences and at the different science forums and he developed significant research and professional relationships in Western, Central and Eastern Europe.

He died on 3 April 1974 in Budapest due to chronic and serious illness.

==Achievements==
His three main fields of interest are in [[Algebra]]: theory of [[Abelian group]]s, theory of [[Module (mathematics)|Modules]] and theory of [[Ring (mathematics)|Rings]]. He was also interested in the [[history of mathematics]].

He revealed the [[direct sum]] of modules and developed the general theory of [[linear equation]]s.

He also made big and important discoveries about [[Radical of a ring|Radicals of Rings]].

He dealt with the problems of [[cardinality]] in [[set theory]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Kertesz.html |title=Andor Kertész |accessdate=2019-02-17 |author=J J O'Connor |author2=E F Robertson |author2-link=Edmund F. Robertson |name-list-style=amp |publisher=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]], School of Mathematics and Statistics. [[University of St Andrews]], [[Scotland]]}}</ref>

During his visiting professorship in [[Halle (Saale)|Halle]], [[East Germany]] he contributed to the discovery of the mathematical achievements of [[Georg Cantor]], too.

He was the important [[scholar]] of the Debrecen algebraic school founded by [[Tibor Szele]].

At the [[Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg]] he had a great role in the establishment of the [[Abstract algebra|Modern algebraic]] school.

==Family==
His father, Lajos Kertész (1899–1974) was a teacher of music. His mother was Mária Nyíri. He had three siblings. Andor Kertész's wife was Ilona Tóth, teacher of history and geography. They had two children, a daughter, physician Gabriella Kertész and a son, linguist András Kertész.

==Selected works==
===Papers===
*Kertész, Andor: On the groups every subgroup of which is a direct summand, ''Publicationes Mathematicae'' 2, Debrecen, 74–75, 1951.
*{{cite journal|author =Kertész, Andor–[[Tibor Szele|Szele, Tibor]]|title= On abelian groups every multiple of which is a direct summand : To Professor Reinhold Baer on his 50th birthday|journal=Acta Scientiarum Mathematicarum|pages=157–166|year=1951|volume=14|location=Szeged|url=http://pub.acta.hu/acta/showCustomerArticle.action?id=6151&dataObjectType=article&returnAction=showCustomerVolume&sessionDataSetId=1c605798e818cfb2&style=|accessdate=2019-02-18}}
*Kertész, Andor: On the decomposibility of abelian ''p''-groups into the direct sum of cyclic groups, ''Acta Mathematica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae'' 3, 121–126, 1952.
*Kertész, Andor–Szele, Tibor: On the smallest distance of two lines in 3-space, ''Publicationes Mathematicae'' 2, Debrecen, 308–309, 1952.
*Kertész, Andor: On fully decomposible abelian torsion groups, ''Acta Mathematica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae'' 3, 225–232, 1952.
*Kertész, Andor: Systems of equations over modules : To Professor Alexander Kurosh on hit 50th birthday. ''Acta scientiarum mathematicarum'', (18) 3–4. pp.&nbsp;207–234. (1957)<ref>{{cite web |url= http://acta.bibl.u-szeged.hu/13835/|title= Egyetemi Kiadványok |accessdate=2019-02-18 |last= |first= |publisher=[[University of Szeged]]}}</ref>
*Kertész, Andor: On independent sets of elements in algebra : To Professor L. Rédei on his 60th birthday. ''Acta scientiarum mathematicarum'', (21) 3–4. pp.&nbsp;260–269. (1960)
*Kertész, Andor: On multimodules, ''Archiv der Mathematik'' 13, 267–274, 1962.
*Kertész, Andor: A new proof of Litoff's theorem, ''Acta Mathematica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae'' 23, 1–3, 1972.

===Books===
*Kertész, Andor: ''Vorlesungen über Artinsche Ringe'', Akadémiai Kiadó, Budapest; Teubner Verlag, Leipzig, 1968.
*Kertész, Andor: ''Einführung in die transfinite Algebra'', Akadémiai Kiadó, Budapest, 1975. {{ISBN|963-05-0382-4}}
*Kertész, Andor–[[Manfred Stern]]: ''Georg Cantor 1845–1918'', Schöpfer der Mengenlehre, [[Halle an der Saale|Halle]], 1983.
*Kertész, Andor: ''Lectures on Artian Rings'', Akadémiai Kiadó, Budapest, 1987.
